slice: FULL SAIL Stage 1 NIGHTWATCH Ch4 Slice C1

findings.red: After 088-095, an arbitrary LOGIN with only ambient public-schema USAGE can EXECUTE public-schema functions that still default-grant PUBLIC (pgcrypto, trigger helpers, business functions). Direct ACL audit cannot see PUBLIC. Trusted-precreated pregrant audit therefore refuses adoption.
findings.green: Canonical 096, run as the queue table/function owner, REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC. A LOGIN with only ambient public USAGE cannot execute any non-explicit public-schema function except the frozen catalog-proven stock pgcrypto 1.3 computational residual. Function owners keep implicit EXECUTE. Existing explicit GRANT EXECUTE to named roles survive. 096 does not GRANT the worker or name live roles/UUIDs.

findings.red: PostgreSQL default privileges keep granting EXECUTE to PUBLIC on newly created functions, so a later CREATE FUNCTION or CREATE EXTENSION by the same owner reopens ambient execute.
findings.green: 096 ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE <applying owner> IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC. Existing and newly created functions owned by that role default non-PUBLIC. Owner nuance: default privileges do not bind another owner; an extension script that GRANT EXECUTE TO PUBLIC explicitly can reintroduce ambient execute. The principal ambient audit still fail-closes on reintroduction unless the same frozen pgcrypto 1.3 catalog proof matches. Procedures are outside ALL FUNCTIONS.

findings.red: Live Sunset staging trusted-precreated worker adoption correctly refused because pregrant audit found dozens of effective public-schema functions callable through ambient PUBLIC EXECUTE. The worker LOGIN stayed parked NOLOGIN with no mapping/grants.
findings.green: After 096, automation principal audit/adoption permits only the contract allowlist plus the frozen catalog-proven pgcrypto 1.3 residual. That residual is computational only and confers no database read/write authority. Re-GRANT EXECUTE TO PUBLIC on any non-allowlisted public-schema function is still rejected as EXCESS_EXECUTE. No runtime flags, provider, or live role changes.

findings.red: Reviewed 096 on exact-master 3144efb8 rolled back atomically on Sunset: REVOKE ALL FUNCTIONS cannot touch 36 public-schema pgcrypto members owned by a different role, the applying owner has no grant option, and 096 fail-closed on any remaining PUBLIC execute. Ledger 096 remains absent. Adding 097 cannot help because 096 never applies.
findings.green: 096 still revokes every function it can. Remaining PUBLIC-executable public-schema routines fail closed unless they are the frozen stock pgcrypto 1.3 signatures proven by catalogs as extension members with exact version 1.3, prokind=f, LANGUAGE c, not SECURITY DEFINER, no dangerous proconfig, and expected volatility/strictness. Owner name is not trusted. Fake same-name, non-member, wrong version/properties, extra members, and arbitrary PUBLIC functions fail atomically. DOWN remains refusal-only.
